article_text:
冨永愛の伝統to未来 第二章～ニッポンの伝統文化を未来へ紡ぐ～

サブタイトル：鎚起銅器①（ついきどうき）

放送日時：2026年10月28日(水)夜10時～10時30分

放送局：BS日テレ

出演者：冨永愛

クレジット：ⒸＢＳ日テレ

番組概要:冨永愛が全国各地を訪ね、その土地に根付く「伝統文化」を紹介します。先人たちから受け継がれてきた「伝統」の素晴らしさを伝えるとともに、後継者問題など伝統文化が置かれている「現状」、そして進むべき「未来」を探っていきます。

番組ホームページ： https://www.bs4.jp/dentotomirai/ 番組公式X： https://x.com/dentou_mirai 番組公式Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@dentoumirai 番組公式TikTok： https://www.tiktok.com/@dentoumirai 番組公式インスタグラム： https://www.instagram.com/bs4_dentou_mirai/

新潟・燕市で２００年以上の歴史

今回、愛さんが訪れるのは、「金属産業のまち」として知られる新潟県燕市。200年以上の歴史を持つ「玉川堂」で、伝統工芸・鎚起銅器（ついきどうき）の魅力を探っていきます。２回にわたり紹介します。

鎚起銅器は一枚の銅板を金槌で叩き打ち縮めることで、立体的な器へと仕上げる工芸品。驚くほど滑らかで美しい光沢を放ち、使い込むほどに銅ならではの経年変化で、味わい深い色を醸し出すことが特徴です。

日用品として幅広く愛好

錆びにくく殺菌作用もある素材としても知られ、最近ではその熱伝導率の高さから、やかんや急須だけでなく、鍋やフライパン、ぐい呑やビールカップ、コーヒーのドリッパーなどの日用品として幅広く愛されています。

そんな鎚起銅器を作る職人たちの技を七代目・玉川基行さんの案内で、間近に見ていきます。 そこには1か月以上もかかるほど、熟練の職人による繊細な技術が隠されていました。

さらに、「見たらどの工房の作品かわかる」ほど、多彩な色を生み出す着色の工程も見学。

そんな鎚起銅器の豆皿作りに愛さんも挑戦。 果たして、無事に作り上げることはできるのでしょうか？ (美術展ナビ編集班)

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Benrubi Gallery 宣布 Christopher Payne 的“In Service”。这是与 MTA Arts and Design 合作的全城展示。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“In Service: MTA Photographs by Christopher Payne”是 MTA Arts & Design 首个全系统摄影展。它为乘客提供了一个难得的幕后视角，得以一窥纽约交通系统，并聚焦于每天维持其运转的技术工人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为这项特别委托，Payne 获得了前所未有的准入机会，得以进入多个 MTA 机构及车辆合作伙伴的维修车间、制造厂房和运营空间。由此产生的照片以惊人的美感和细节，揭示了 MTA 核心那些不为人知的劳动。“In Service”以 52 个大型灯箱呈现，是 Arts & Design 迄今规模最大的摄影装置，也是首次有单一摄影师的作品在整个交通系统中同步展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过鲜明、构图考究的图像，展览突显了维护和制造系统关键部件的劳动者的专业与奉献。为捕捉这一基础设施及其错综复杂的网络，Payne 常常以长时间内多次曝光合成图像。这种细致的方法赋予他的照片一种平静、静止的质感——尽管工业环境中有活动和声响，他的拍摄对象和工业题材往往传达出这种质感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览在曼哈顿和布鲁克林的五个车站展出，按主题组织，以反映这个幕后世界的广度。在 Grand Central Madison，照片展现了 MTA 五个运营机构中大规模的服务，揭示运营的规模以及其中人的存在。在 Grand Central Terminal Dining Concourse，在维护和制造空间拍摄的工人肖像让系统基础设施所投入的关怀更具人情味，并加以颂扬。42 St-Bryant Park 的装置呈现日常部件，通过 Payne 独特的视觉手法重新审视。在 Bowling Green，观众可以跟随巴士制造与维护的各个阶段——从车架焊接到无障碍坡道组装，再到每条线路结束时最后的巴士清洗。在 Atlantic Av-Barclays Ctr，地铁车厢的生命周期被追溯：从目前在内布拉斯加州生产的川崎 R211 车厢，到在扬克斯测试，再到在翻修车间维护。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“In Service: MTA Photographs by Christopher Payne”由 MTA Arts & Design 经理 Maggie Murtha 策展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览地点", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "42 St-Bryant Park", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Atlantic Av-Barclays Ctr", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bowling Green", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Grand Central Terminal Dining Concourse", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Grand Central Madison", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Benrubi Gallery 529 W 20th St Fl 8 New York, NY 10011 www.benrubigallery.com", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Benrubi Gallery announced Christopher Payne ’s “In Service.” A city-wide presentation with the MTA Arts and Design .

“In Service: MTA Photographs by Christopher Payne” is MTA Arts & Design’s first systemwide photography exhibition. It offers riders a rare, behind-the-scenes look at New York’s transit system, spotlighting the skilled workers who keep it running every day.

For this special commission, Payne had unprecedented access to repair shops, manufacturing floors, and operational spaces at multiple MTA agencies and rolling stock partners. The resulting photographs reveal the unseen labor at the heart of the MTA with striking beauty and detail. Presented across 52 large lightboxes, “In Service” is the most extensive photography installation undertaken by Arts & Design and the first time a single photographer’s work has been showcased simultaneously throughout the transit system.

Through vivid, thoughtfully composed images, the exhibition highlights the expertise and dedication of the workforce that maintains and manufactures the system’s essential components. To capture this infrastructure and its intricate networks, Payne often creates composite images built from multiple exposures taken over extended periods. This meticulous approach gives his photographs the calm, still quality that his sitters and industrial subjects often convey, despite the activity and sounds of their industrial surroundings.

Displayed in five stations in Manhattan and Brooklyn, the exhibition is organized into themes that reflect the breadth of this behind-the-scenes world. At Grand Central Madison, photographs illustrate service at scale within the MTA’s five operating agencies, revealing the magnitude of operations and the human presence within them. At Grand Central Terminal Dining Concourse, worker portraits taken in maintenance and manufacturing spaces humanize and celebrate the care invested in the system’s infrastructure. The 42 St-Bryant Park installation features everyday components, reconsidered through Payne’s distinct visual approach. At Bowling Green, viewers can follow the stages of bus manufacturing and maintenance—from frame welding and the assembling of accessibility ramps to the final bus wash at the end of each route. At Atlantic Av-Barclays Ctr, the lifecycle of subway cars is traced from Kawasaki R211 cars currently in production in Nebraska to testing in Yonkers and maintenance in overhaul shops.

“In Service: MTA Photographs by Christopher Payne” is curated by MTA Arts & Design Manager Maggie Murtha.

Exhibition Locations

42 St-Bryant Park

Atlantic Av-Barclays Ctr

Bowling Green

Grand Central Terminal Dining Concourse

Grand Central Madison

Benrubi Gallery 529 W 20th St Fl 8 New York, NY 10011 www.benrubigallery.com

title_original: La Bola Negra Review: Queer Epic Feels Like a Long-Lost Novel
editorial_title_zh: 《黑球》影评：酷儿史诗宛如一部失落已久的小说
editorial_excerpt_zh: 注：这篇影评最初发表于我们2026年戛纳电影节报道期间。该片将于10月16日在院线上映。如果说19世纪和20世纪的叙事由宏大的文学定义，那么21世纪则完全属于电影。我们阅读减少，观看增多；因此，电影……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "注：这篇影评最初发表于我们2026年戛纳电影节报道期间。该片将于10月16日在院线上映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/tfs-criticspick-star-orange.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果说19世纪和20世纪的叙事由宏大的文学定义，那么21世纪则完全属于电影。我们阅读减少，观看增多；因此，电影已成为交织着各种时间线和主角的宏大故事的替代品。在这方面最新的作品是戛纳的惊艳之作《黑球》（La Bola Negra，又名 The Black Ball ），这是一个真正雄心勃勃的项目——它受历史真相启发，同时又是一部虚构的、极具个人色彩的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部由哈维尔·卡尔沃（Javier Calvo）和哈维尔·安布罗斯（Javier Ambrossi，也被称为 Los Javis）执导的西班牙剧情片，讲述了三个男人的命运，他们的命运因对身份、性和爱的追寻而紧密相连。在1932年，年轻的卡洛斯（米洛·基费斯 Milo Quifes 饰）在西班牙社会中为自己争取一席之地。在1937年，25岁的塞瓦斯蒂安（西班牙现象级音乐人 Guitarricadelafuente 饰）在求生欲的驱驱使下，置身于西班牙内战之中，并爱上了神秘的拉斐尔（米格尔·贝尔纳多 Miguel Bernardeau 饰）。在2017年，历史学家兼迷失灵魂的阿尔韦托（卡洛斯·冈萨雷斯 Carlos González 饰）在收到一份奇怪的手稿后，直面他已故祖父的遗产。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一情节的灵感源自费德里科·加西亚·洛尔卡（Federico García Lorca）的一部未竟剧作，《黑球》（La Bola Negra）这个独特的片名便取自于此。按照1930年代西班牙的投票程序，由于性取向而收到黑球（而非白球）意味着一个人遭到“赌场”（Casino——一个享有声望的社交俱乐部）的拒绝。在遭受残忍谋杀之前，这位西班牙诗人仅写下了该剧的四页。然而，多亏了两位导演，洛尔卡的剧本如今通过电影的篇幅得以延伸，卡尔沃和安布罗斯运用并重塑过去，拼凑出了他们自己版本的真相。在这个框架内，《黑球》将虚构与历史人物、内战（发生在1936年至1939年之间）令人发指的恐怖，以及酷儿不再被视为威胁的相对和平时期（设定于2017年的现代故事线）交织在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "表面看来，这些故事之间唯一的联系便是角色身上显而易见的酷儿特质，这种特质表现在他们注视其他男人的方式、坠入爱河的方式，或是他们如何成为随之而来的孤独之牺牲品（尤其是在以保守的1930年代西班牙为背景的两条叙事中）。正如这部同名剧作一样，这部史诗般厚重的戏剧——用在片中饰演一位致力于洛尔卡作品学者的格伦·克洛斯（Glenn Close）的话来说——关乎选择。更准确地说，是一个酷儿的选择。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影巨作触及了无数主题：决定出柜时不可避免要面对的审判（卡洛斯）；在长枪党（Falange）崛起后酷儿波希米亚主义消亡感（卡洛斯和塞瓦斯蒂安）；无论你是否愿意、都无法避免地继承的代际家庭创伤（阿尔韦托）；以及揭示自己真实身份的行为（每个人）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "后一点在另一个令人难忘的客串中得到了呼应：独一无二的佩内洛普·克鲁兹（Penélope Cruz）的表演性演出。作为虚构的表演者内内·罗梅罗（Nené Romero），她以其永恒的风度启迪了观众。她和塞瓦斯蒂安就伪装的行为展开了一场辛酸的对话：罗梅罗提到她有一个朋友可以假扮成任何人，甚至包括拉热尔·梅勒（Raquel Meller，该时代著名的西班牙歌手和表演者）。主角的酷儿特质并没有被生硬地对峙——它存在于勇敢士兵的外表之下——但罗梅罗心知肚明；她在她表演时他眼中的最初火花中看到了这一点。这是他所寻求的“变装”（drag）：在一个充满淫荡男人的房间里，塞瓦斯蒂安是唯一一个不把她当成性对象的人。“异装癖是对可能性的幻想。战争则恰恰相反，”她向他解释道。这个片段与许多其他片段一样，让细微差别浮出水面。在《黑球》中，一切都在字里行间或通过诗意的寓言诉说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影也加入当代电影的行列，渴望通过视听手段实现小说化的叙事。去年的《坠落之声》（Sound of Falling）有着类似的前提，呼应了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫（Virginia Woolf）和威廉·福克纳（William Faulkner）等有影响力的现代主义作家，用图像而非文学创造了一种挑衅性的意识流。在这里，“奇观电影”（cinema of attractions）类似于马里奥·巴尔加斯·略萨（Mario Vargas Llosa）1969年的小说《酒吧长谈》（Conversation in the Cathedral）的风格，每个序列都为这个等式增添了另一层含义。由观众来决定他们何时以及如何解码这个令人印象深刻的拼图。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种确实具有感染力的效果，得到了劳尔·雷弗雷（Raül Refree）非画外音管弦配乐的支撑，该配乐频繁使用西班牙吉他和小号。这一音乐元素通过提醒人们爱与激情永远不应被遗忘（即便被埋没在战争的废墟或时间的流逝之下），巩固了《黑球》的精神内核。它唤起了人们对过去的怀旧之情——那过去或许早已消逝，但无论如何都可以通过电影重新找回。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“你不觉得搞笑吗？你唯一不在乎的故事竟然是你自己的？”阿尔伯托的伴侣在某个时刻问道。这句话可以双重解读。的确，我们得知阿尔伯托通过沉浸在别人的故事中来逃避自己的过去——与母亲紧张的关系，以及他从未见过祖父的事实。这大概就是他决定成为一名历史学家和作家的原因。但对观众来说同样如此：为了银幕上的娱乐，人们常常逃避痛苦的和解。《黑球》让我们意识到，不论后果如何，是时候正视我们自己的生活了。我们都可以在电影中迷失自我，但正如杰出的波兰小说家维斯瓦夫·米斯利维夫斯基（Wiesław Myśliwski）所言，生活和“最重要的人类”才是最重要的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在长达155分钟的不朽片长中，摄影师格里斯·霍达纳（Gris Jordana）的镜头追踪着我们的主角，宛如一位试图重修旧好的旧日恋人。它贴近他们身体的程度，就像亲密接触时恋人的双手——那些特大特写就像是轻抚并安抚人心的手掌。卡尔沃和塞巴斯蒂安或许只是过去的迴响，但《黑球》在阿尔伯托的微小帮助下，将他们从厄运和记忆的不可靠性所导致的磨灭中拯救出来。这是一份只有电影通过模仿和视觉化才能赋予我们的生命之礼。这些字符在当下和我们体内保持着活力，散发着一种类似于这部轰动电影中经常诵读的加西亚·洛尔卡台词的那种肯定生命的品质。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《黑球》在2026年戛纳电影节上首映，并将由Netflix发行。", "translated": true}]

The film opens in theaters on October 16."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/tfs-criticspick-star-orange.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "If 19th- and 20th-century storytelling was defined by grandiose literature, the 21st is all about cinema. We read less and watch more; consequently, films have become a substitute for sweeping stories that weave various timelines and protagonists. The latest in such regard is Cannes revelation La Bola Negra (aka The Black Ball ), a truly ambitious project—inspired by historical truth while remaining a fictional, highly personal undertaking."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Spanish drama, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (also known as Los Javis), follows three men whose fates are bound by a search for identity, sexuality, and love. In 1932, young Carlos (Milo Quifes) fights for his place in Spanish society. In 1937, 25-year-old Sebastián (Spanish phenomenon Guitarricadelafuente), driven by the desire to survive, finds himself amidst the Spanish Civil War and falls in love with the mysterious Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau). In 2017, Alberto (Carlos González), a historian and lost soul, confronts his late grandfather’s legacy after receiving a strange manuscript."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This plot is inspired by Federico García Lorca’s unfinished play from which La Bola Negra takes its peculiar title. Per the voting process in 1930s Spain, receiving black balls (instead of white ones) meant the rejection of a man from a “Casino”—a prestigious social club—due to his sexual orientation. Before being brutally murdered, the Spanish poet managed to write only four pages of the play. Yet, thanks to the directors, Lorca’s manuscript is now extended by cinematic pages, Calvo and Ambrossi assembling their own version of truth by using the past and reinventing it. Within this framework, La Bola Negra blends fictional and historical characters with the appalling terror of the civil conflict (taking place between 1936 and 1939) and more peaceful times (the modern storyline set in 2017), when being queer is no longer considered a threat."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Seemingly, the only connection between these stories is the characters’ evident queerness, which can be spotted in the way they look at other men, how they fall in love, or how they become victims of the loneliness that accompanies it (especially in the two narratives taking place in conservative 1930s Spain). Just like the eponymous play, this epic and robust drama is—to quote Glenn Close’s character, who plays a scholar invested in Lorca’s work—about choice. A queer choice, to be more precise."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There are myriad themes tackled by this giant of a film: the inevitable judgment one faces when deciding to come out (Carlos); the sense of an ending for queer bohemia after the rise of the Falange (both Carlos and Sebastián); the generational family trauma inherited whether you like it or not (Alberto); and the act of revealing one’s true identity (everyone)."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The latter is echoed in another memorable cameo: a performative act from the one and only Penélope Cruz. As Nené Romero, a fictionalized performer, she enlightens the audience with her timeless élan. She and Sebastián have a poignant conversation about the act of pretense: Romero mentions she has a friend who can pretend to be anyone, even Raquel Meller (a famous Spanish diseuse and performer of the era). The main character’s queerness is not bluntly confronted—it exists beneath the facade of a brave soldier—but Romero understands everything; she saw it in the very first spark in his eyes during her performance. It is the “drag” he seeks: in a room full of lascivious men, Sebastián is the only one who does not treat her as a sexual object. “Transvestism is the fantasy of possibility. War is the opposite,” she explains to him. This sequence, like many others, allows nuance to rise to the surface. In La Bola Negra , everything is spoken between the lines or through poetic allegories."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The film also joins a lineage of contemporary cinema that aspires to novelistic storytelling through audiovisual means. Last year’s Sound of Falling had a similar premise, echoing influential modernist writers like Virginia Woolf and William Faulkner to create a provocative stream of consciousness through images rather than literature. Here, the “cinema of attractions” resembles the style of Mario Vargas Llosa’s 1969 novel Conversation in the Cathedral , each sequence adding another layer of meaning to the equation. It is for the spectator to decide when and how they will decode this impressive jigsaw."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "That effect, indeed affecting, is bolstered by Raül Refree’s non-diegetic, orchestral score, which makes frequent use of Spanish guitars and trumpets. This musical element aids La Bola Negra ‘s ethos by reminding one that love and passion should never be forgotten, even if buried under the debris of war or the passage of time. It evokes nostalgia for a past that may be long gone, but can nonetheless be reclaimed through cinema."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Isn’t it funny that the only story you don’t care about is yours?” Alberto’s partner asks at one point. This can be read dually. It is true: we learn that Alberto escapes from his own past—a strenuous relationship with his mother and the fact that he never met his grandfather—by losing himself in the stories of others. This is supposedly why he decided to become a historian and writer. But the same can be said about the audience, which often runs from painful reconciliations for the sake of onscreen entertainment. La Bola Negra makes us realize it is time to confront our own lives, no matter the consequences. We can all lose ourselves at the movies, but it is life and the “human being who matters most,” as the prominent Polish novelist Wiesław Myśliwski would put it."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Throughout a monumental 155-minute runtime, cinematographer Gris Jordana’s camera tracks our heroes like an old lover seeking to reconcile. It is as near their bodies as a lover’s hands during an intimate encounter—the close-ups are like palms that caress and soothe. Carlos and Sebastián might be echoes of the past, but La Bola Negra , with a little help from Alberto, rescues them from being obliterated by misfortune and the unreliability of memory. It is a vital gift that only cinema, through the act of imitation and visualization, can bestow upon us. These characters stay alive within the moment and within us, exuding a life-affirming quality akin to García Lorca’s lines so often uttered in this sensational film."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La Bola Negra premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival and will be released by Netflix."}]

Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 Cannes coverage. The film opens in theaters on October 16.

If 19th- and 20th-century storytelling was defined by grandiose literature, the 21st is all about cinema. We read less and watch more; consequently, films have become a substitute for sweeping stories that weave various timelines and protagonists. The latest in such regard is Cannes revelation La Bola Negra (aka The Black Ball ), a truly ambitious project—inspired by historical truth while remaining a fictional, highly personal undertaking.

The Spanish drama, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (also known as Los Javis), follows three men whose fates are bound by a search for identity, sexuality, and love. In 1932, young Carlos (Milo Quifes) fights for his place in Spanish society. In 1937, 25-year-old Sebastián (Spanish phenomenon Guitarricadelafuente), driven by the desire to survive, finds himself amidst the Spanish Civil War and falls in love with the mysterious Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau). In 2017, Alberto (Carlos González), a historian and lost soul, confronts his late grandfather’s legacy after receiving a strange manuscript.

This plot is inspired by Federico García Lorca’s unfinished play from which La Bola Negra takes its peculiar title. Per the voting process in 1930s Spain, receiving black balls (instead of white ones) meant the rejection of a man from a “Casino”—a prestigious social club—due to his sexual orientation. Before being brutally murdered, the Spanish poet managed to write only four pages of the play. Yet, thanks to the directors, Lorca’s manuscript is now extended by cinematic pages, Calvo and Ambrossi assembling their own version of truth by using the past and reinventing it. Within this framework, La Bola Negra blends fictional and historical characters with the appalling terror of the civil conflict (taking place between 1936 and 1939) and more peaceful times (the modern storyline set in 2017), when being queer is no longer considered a threat.

Seemingly, the only connection between these stories is the characters’ evident queerness, which can be spotted in the way they look at other men, how they fall in love, or how they become victims of the loneliness that accompanies it (especially in the two narratives taking place in conservative 1930s Spain). Just like the eponymous play, this epic and robust drama is—to quote Glenn Close’s character, who plays a scholar invested in Lorca’s work—about choice. A queer choice, to be more precise.

There are myriad themes tackled by this giant of a film: the inevitable judgment one faces when deciding to come out (Carlos); the sense of an ending for queer bohemia after the rise of the Falange (both Carlos and Sebastián); the generational family trauma inherited whether you like it or not (Alberto); and the act of revealing one’s true identity (everyone).

The latter is echoed in another memorable cameo: a performative act from the one and only Penélope Cruz. As Nené Romero, a fictionalized performer, she enlightens the audience with her timeless élan. She and Sebastián have a poignant conversation about the act of pretense: Romero mentions she has a friend who can pretend to be anyone, even Raquel Meller (a famous Spanish diseuse and performer of the era). The main character’s queerness is not bluntly confronted—it exists beneath the facade of a brave soldier—but Romero understands everything; she saw it in the very first spark in his eyes during her performance. It is the “drag” he seeks: in a room full of lascivious men, Sebastián is the only one who does not treat her as a sexual object. “Transvestism is the fantasy of possibility. War is the opposite,” she explains to him. This sequence, like many others, allows nuance to rise to the surface. In La Bola Negra , everything is spoken between the lines or through poetic allegories.

The film also joins a lineage of contemporary cinema that aspires to novelistic storytelling through audiovisual means. Last year’s Sound of Falling had a similar premise, echoing influential modernist writers like Virginia Woolf and William Faulkner to create a provocative stream of consciousness through images rather than literature. Here, the “cinema of attractions” resembles the style of Mario Vargas Llosa’s 1969 novel Conversation in the Cathedral , each sequence adding another layer of meaning to the equation. It is for the spectator to decide when and how they will decode this impressive jigsaw.

That effect, indeed affecting, is bolstered by Raül Refree’s non-diegetic, orchestral score, which makes frequent use of Spanish guitars and trumpets. This musical element aids La Bola Negra ‘s ethos by reminding one that love and passion should never be forgotten, even if buried under the debris of war or the passage of time. It evokes nostalgia for a past that may be long gone, but can nonetheless be reclaimed through cinema.

“Isn’t it funny that the only story you don’t care about is yours?” Alberto’s partner asks at one point. This can be read dually. It is true: we learn that Alberto escapes from his own past—a strenuous relationship with his mother and the fact that he never met his grandfather—by losing himself in the stories of others. This is supposedly why he decided to become a historian and writer. But the same can be said about the audience, which often runs from painful reconciliations for the sake of onscreen entertainment. La Bola Negra makes us realize it is time to confront our own lives, no matter the consequences. We can all lose ourselves at the movies, but it is life and the “human being who matters most,” as the prominent Polish novelist Wiesław Myśliwski would put it.

Throughout a monumental 155-minute runtime, cinematographer Gris Jordana’s camera tracks our heroes like an old lover seeking to reconcile. It is as near their bodies as a lover’s hands during an intimate encounter—the close-ups are like palms that caress and soothe. Carlos and Sebastián might be echoes of the past, but La Bola Negra , with a little help from Alberto, rescues them from being obliterated by misfortune and the unreliability of memory. It is a vital gift that only cinema, through the act of imitation and visualization, can bestow upon us. These characters stay alive within the moment and within us, exuding a life-affirming quality akin to García Lorca’s lines so often uttered in this sensational film.

La Bola Negra premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival and will be released by Netflix.

title_original: Francesco Bonami è stato nominato direttore artistico della Casa della Cultura GES-2 di Mosca
editorial_title_zh: 弗朗切斯科·博纳米被任命为莫斯科 GES-2 文化之家艺术总监
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在西方与俄罗斯文化关系复杂的阶段，博纳米旨在为亿万富翁列昂尼德·米赫尔松旗下的 V-A-C 基金会资助的机构“挑选最佳项目”。文章《弗朗切斯科·博纳米被任命为艺术总监……》
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "弗朗切斯科·博纳米（Francesco Bonami）是一位拥有美国国籍的意大利策展人，自2021年起担任该机构的战略顾问，现已被任命为莫斯科 V-A-C 基金会（V-A-C Foundation）推介的文化中心 GES-2 文化之家（GES-2 House of Culture）的艺术总监。在新职务中，博纳米将与策展团队合作，指导节目编排并开发艺术项目，与团队共同进行项目的遴选与开发。与自2022年起担任节目总监的俄罗斯策展人阿利萨·普鲁德尼科娃（Alisa Prudnikova）的角色交接预计于2026年12月6日进行，尽管普鲁德尼科娃自2027年起将以独立策展人身份继续合作，在多年来拓展了研究活动与国际合作后，专注于文化之家的学术研究与国际驻留项目。然而，这一任命正值俄西方文化关系面临复杂阶段：自2022年2月试图入侵乌克兰的战争重启以来，俄罗斯与欧洲机构之间的合作一直受到政治和机构层面的性质诘问，同时大量国际交流与项目也已被暂停。", "links": [{"text": "è stato nominato", "url": "https://cdn.v-a-c.org/v-a-c-static/store/document/870/file/7752c2d242b745f6599bf9452f9ead4c.pdf"}, {"text": "GES-2 House of Culture", "url": "https://ges-2.org/en"}, {"text": "Mosca", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/mosca/"}, {"text": "V-A-C Foundation", "url": "https://v-a-c.org/en"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在任命官方公告中，博纳米表示：“在我看来，艺术总监的角色在于催化艺术能量。我们共同的目标是为 GES-2 挑选最好的项目。我的经验应该会在这个方向上有所帮助。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "谁是弗朗切斯科·博纳米", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "弗朗切斯科·博纳米1955年出生于佛罗伦萨，是一位策展人和艺术评论家。他在博物馆机构与大型国际活动之间奔走，构建了自己的职业生涯，其中包括于1995年至2018年担任都灵桑德雷托·雷·雷巴登戈基金会（Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo）艺术总监，以及于1999年至2008年担任芝加哥当代艺术博物馆（Museum of Contemporary Art）高级策展人。2003年，他执导了第50届威尼斯双年展；2000年，他参与策划了卢布尔雅那 Manifesta 3；2010年，他参与策划了纽约惠特尼双年展（Whitney Biennial）。他的职业轨迹在评论活动与普及项目之间展开，并关注当代艺术语言的变革以及作品与公众建立联系的方式。", "links": [{"text": "Francesco Bonami", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/francesco-bonami/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/francesco-bonami-n-1024x810.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "弗朗切斯科·博纳米", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他与俄罗斯艺术界的渊源始于2010年和2011年，当时博纳米与伊rene·卡尔代罗尼（Irene Calderoni）共同策划了《Modernikon. Contemporary Art From Russia》，这是一场在都灵和威尼斯展出的致力于俄罗斯当代艺术的展览。2017年，V-A-C 出版社（V-A-C Press）用俄语出版了他的著作《我也会做！》（Lo potevo fare anch’io!），该书致力于理解当代艺术以及作品与观众之间往往伴随的困难。随后在2024年，博纳米与泽菲拉·特古洛娃（Zelfira Tregulova）共同策划了《Square and Space. From Malevich to GES-2》项目，该项目将前卫派遗产与莫斯科机构的历史和身份联系在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当时，博纳米表示：“我和 V-A-C 基金会的合作与友谊从2008年开始，已有16年之久，从未中断过。所以我并不是被‘吸引’来的，也不是被莫斯科吸引，而是被一个文化项目吸引，它依然是希望的少数几个地区之一。由伦佐·皮亚诺（Renzo Piano）和 Rpbw 设计的 Ges2 是一个充满活力的地方，自开业以来已有超过一百万人参观，他们在内部找到了无与伦比的宁静和文化供给。破坏或中断对话和文化交流一直意味着放弃任何和平的希望。作为一名策展人，我感到自己对年轻一代负有保持这种对话开放的责任，无论我可能承担什么风险，无论是职业上的还是个人上的。我的决定不是一个选择，而简然是一个智识上的义务。该展览将是对艺术品、建筑与社会空间之间关系变革的宏大反思。从激进的手势到自拍文化。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "GES-2 文化之家，从发电厂到文化中心", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "GES-2 于2021年12月4日向公众开放，位于莫斯科市中心博洛特纳亚（Bolotnaya）河岸的一座20世纪初的前发电厂空间内，正对克里姆林宫，这是一座经伦佐·皮亚诺工作室设计改造为致力于当代文化制作与传播的中心的建筑。“文化之家”（House of Culture）这一名称让人联想起旧苏联时期历史上旨在接待艺术、培训、戏剧和电影活动的“文化宫”模式。GES-2 以当代视角对其进行了重新诠释，其节目保持了多学科交叉的特点，将视觉艺术、表演、音乐、工坊活动以及面向公众的倡议联系起来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "V-A-C 基金会", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该空间由 V-A-C 基金会开发，该基金会由俄罗斯天然气行业领军企业诺瓦泰克（Novatek）负责人、能源行业企业家列昂尼德·米赫尔松（Leonid Mikhelson）于2009年在莫斯科创立。基金会致力于推动艺术实验和当代文化的传播，并在境外开展活动，其中包括威尼斯扎特雷宫（Palazzo Zattere）所举办的项目。然而，其创始人的背景引发了关于私人资助与文化自主之间关系的问题：米赫尔松是一位天然气大亨、俄罗斯经济界的核心人物，也被认为与总统弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）关系密切。基金会的私人属性并未使其脱离其运营所在的经济和政治环境；相反，支持该文化项目的资源来自与其俄罗斯经济战略部门紧密相关的活动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2022年，时任基金会艺术总监弗朗切斯科·马纳科尔达（Francesco Manacorda）因俄罗斯对乌克兰的军事行动而离任，威尼斯扎特雷宫（Palazzo Zattere）基地的活动也被暂停。而莫斯科的 GES-2 则继续运营。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "战争爆发后不久，冰岛艺术家拉格纳·基亚尔滕松（Ragnar Kjartansson）也取消了原定在 GES-2 推出的行为表演，并声明：“在恐怖开始之际，不可能呈现这项作品。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "新任管理层与未来项目", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在新职位上，博纳米将与策展团队合作挑选和开发项目，为已经启动的项目规划保持连续性。已宣布的项目包括定于2026年12月举办、由博纳米与德米特里·别尔金（Dmitry Belkin）共同策划的《Things, Idols, Bananas》。未来三年的主题方向和项目将于年底前公布，新管理层将需要面对一个不断演变的规划，在保持艺术创作与研究之间关系的同时，也兼顾该中心所标榜的、对不同艺术语言的开放性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2022年2月之后，与俄罗斯机构合作的可能性已成为艺术家、策展人、博物馆和活动组织者共同面临的一项争议话题。未来三年的艺术选择将如何应对该中心运营所处的环境、以及该项目的国际维度能保留多大的空间，仍有待观察。如果说与俄罗斯的微妙关系一直是今年双年展期间备受关注、并引发抗议与示威的话题，那么博纳米的任命则再次强力开启了这一篇章，并继续引发艺术界对一个文化项目在何种程度上、以及如何才能真正独立于为其提供经济和政治基础的结构之外的思考。", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Francesco Bonami , curatore italiano con cittadinanza statunitense e già consulente strategico dell’istituzione dal 2021, è stato nominato direttore artistico di GES-2 House of Culture , il centro culturale di Mosca promosso dalla V-A-C Foundation . Nel nuovo incarico, Bonami contribuirà a orientare la programmazione e a sviluppare i progetti artistici insieme al gruppo curatoriale, lavorando con il team alla selezione e allo sviluppo dei progetti. Il passaggio di ruolo con Alisa Prudnikova , curatrice russa e Programme Director dal 2022, è previsto per il 6 dicembre 2026, anche se dal 2027 Prudnikova proseguirà la collaborazione come curatrice indipendente, concentrandosi su studi accademici e residenze internazionali per House of Culture dopo averne ampliato negli anni attività di ricerca e collaborazioni internazionali. La nomina arriva però in una fase complessa per le relazioni culturali tra Russia e Occidente: dalla ripresa invasione nel tentativo di invadere l’Ucraina nel febbraio 2022, le collaborazioni tra istituzioni russe ed europee sono state investite da interrogativi politici e istituzionali, mentre numerosi scambi e progetti internazionali sono stati sospesi.", "links": [{"text": "è stato nominato", "url": "https://cdn.v-a-c.org/v-a-c-static/store/document/870/file/7752c2d242b745f6599bf9452f9ead4c.pdf"}, {"text": "GES-2 House of Culture", "url": "https://ges-2.org/en"}, {"text": "Mosca", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/mosca/"}, {"text": "V-A-C Foundation", "url": "https://v-a-c.org/en"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nel comunicato ufficiale della nomina, Bonami ha affermato: «A mio avviso, il ruolo di Direttore Artistico consiste nel catalizzare l’energia artistica. Il nostro obiettivo comune è individuare i progetti migliori per il GES-2. La mia esperienza dovrebbe essere d’aiuto in questo senso»."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Chi è Francesco Bonami"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nato a Firenze nel 1955, Francesco Bonami è un curatore e critico d’arte. Ha lavorato muovendosi tra istituzioni museali e grandi manifestazioni internazionali, costruendo una carriera che vede la direzione artistica della Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo di Torino, mantenuta dal 1995 al 2018, e l’incarico di senior curator al Museum of Contemporary Art di Chicago, ricoperto dal 1999 al 2008. Nel 2003 ha diretto la 50ª Biennale di Venezia, mentre nel 2000 ha partecipato alla curatela di Manifesta 3 a Lubiana, e nel 2010 a quella della Whitney Biennial di New York. Il suo percorso si è sviluppato tra attività critica e progetti di divulgazione, con un’attenzione rivolta alle trasformazioni del linguaggio artistico contemporaneo e alle modalità con cui le opere entrano in relazione con il pubblico.", "links": [{"text": "Francesco Bonami", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/francesco-bonami/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/francesco-bonami-n-1024x810.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Francesco Bonami", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il legame con la scena russa ha inizio quando, nel 2010 e nel 2011, Bonami ha curato con Irene Calderoni Modernikon. Contemporary Art From Russia , mostra dedicata all’arte contemporanea russa presentata a Torino e Venezia. Nel 2017 V-A-C Press ha pubblicato in russo il suo libro Lo potevo fare anch’io! , dedicato alla comprensione dell’arte contemporanea e alle difficoltà che spesso accompagnano il rapporto tra opere e spettatori. Nel 2024, poi, Bonami ha curato con Zelfira Tregulova Square and Space. From Malevich to GES-2 , progetto che ha messo in relazione l’eredità dell’avanguardia con la storia e l’identità dell’istituzione moscovita."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In quell’occasione, Bonami ha affermato: «Il mio rapporto di collaborazione e amicizia con la V-A-C Foundation va avanti dal 2008, da 16 anni, e non si è mai interrotto. Non sono stato “attirato” quindi e non da Mosca ma da un progetto culturale che rimane una delle poche zone di speranza. Ges2 disegnata da Renzo Piano e Rpbw è un luogo vitale visitato dalla sua apertura da più di un milione di persone che al suo interno trovano una tranquillità e un’offerta culturale eccezionali. Distruggere o interrompere il dialogo e lo scambio culturale significa da sempre abbandonare ogni speranza di pace. Da curatore sento la responsabilità verso le giovani generazioni di mantenere questo dialogo aperto, non importa il rischio che posso correre, sia professionale che personale. La mia non è una decisione ma banalmente un obbligo intellettuale. La mostra sarà un grande riflessione sulla trasformazione del rapporto fra opera d’arte, architettura e spazio sociale. Dal gesto radicale alla cultura dei selfie»."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "GES-2 House of Culture, da centrale elettrica a centro culturale"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "GES-2 ha aperto al pubblico il 4 dicembre 2021 negli spazi di una ex centrale elettrica dei primi del Novecento situata sull’argine di Bolotnaya, nel centro di Mosca, proprio di fronte al Cremlino, un edificio trasformato su progetto dello studio di Renzo Piano in un centro dedicato alla produzione e alla diffusione della cultura contemporanea. La denominazione “House of Culture” richiama il modello delle “case della cultura”, luoghi storicamente destinati ad accogliere attività artistiche, formative, teatrali e cinematografiche della vecchia Unione Sovietica. GES-2 ne propone una reinterpretazione in chiave contemporanea, con una programmazione che ne mantiene la multidisciplinarietà mettendo in relazione arti visive, performance, musica, attività laboratoriali e iniziative rivolte al pubblico."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "La V-A-C Foundation"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Lo spazio è stato sviluppato dalla V-A-C Foundation, fondata a Mosca nel 2009 da Leonid Mikhelson , imprenditore attivo nel settore energetico e a capo di Novatek, tra i principali produttori di gas naturale in Russia. La Fondazione ha promosso progetti dedicati alla sperimentazione artistica e alla diffusione della cultura contemporanea, sviluppando attività anche fuori dal Paese, tra cui quelle ospitate a Palazzo Zattere, a Venezia. Il profilo del suo fondatore, però, introduce una questione che riguarda il rapporto tra finanziamenti privati e autonomia culturale: Mikhelson è infatti un magnate del gas, una figura di primo piano dell’economia russa ed è considerato vicino al presidente Vladimir Putin . article_text:
Francesco Bonami , curatore italiano con cittadinanza statunitense e già consulente strategico dell’istituzione dal 2021, è stato nominato direttore artistico di GES-2 House of Culture , il centro culturale di Mosca promosso dalla V-A-C Foundation . Nel nuovo incarico, Bonami contribuirà a orientare la programmazione e a sviluppare i progetti artistici insieme al gruppo curatoriale, lavorando con il team alla selezione e allo sviluppo dei progetti. Il passaggio di ruolo con Alisa Prudnikova , curatrice russa e Programme Director dal 2022, è previsto per il 6 dicembre 2026, anche se dal 2027 Prudnikova proseguirà la collaborazione come curatrice indipendente, concentrandosi su studi accademici e residenze internazionali per House of Culture dopo averne ampliato negli anni attività di ricerca e collaborazioni internazionali. La nomina arriva però in una fase complessa per le relazioni culturali tra Russia e Occidente: dalla ripresa invasione nel tentativo di invadere l’Ucraina nel febbraio 2022, le collaborazioni tra istituzioni russe ed europee sono state investite da interrogativi politici e istituzionali, mentre numerosi scambi e progetti internazionali sono stati sospesi.

Nel comunicato ufficiale della nomina, Bonami ha affermato: «A mio avviso, il ruolo di Direttore Artistico consiste nel catalizzare l’energia artistica. Il nostro obiettivo comune è individuare i progetti migliori per il GES-2. La mia esperienza dovrebbe essere d’aiuto in questo senso».

Chi è Francesco Bonami

Nato a Firenze nel 1955, Francesco Bonami è un curatore e critico d’arte. Ha lavorato muovendosi tra istituzioni museali e grandi manifestazioni internazionali, costruendo una carriera che vede la direzione artistica della Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo di Torino, mantenuta dal 1995 al 2018, e l’incarico di senior curator al Museum of Contemporary Art di Chicago, ricoperto dal 1999 al 2008. Nel 2003 ha diretto la 50ª Biennale di Venezia, mentre nel 2000 ha partecipato alla curatela di Manifesta 3 a Lubiana, e nel 2010 a quella della Whitney Biennial di New York. Il suo percorso si è sviluppato tra attività critica e progetti di divulgazione, con un’attenzione rivolta alle trasformazioni del linguaggio artistico contemporaneo e alle modalità con cui le opere entrano in relazione con il pubblico.

Il legame con la scena russa ha inizio quando, nel 2010 e nel 2011, Bonami ha curato con Irene Calderoni Modernikon. Contemporary Art From Russia , mostra dedicata all’arte contemporanea russa presentata a Torino e Venezia. Nel 2017 V-A-C Press ha pubblicato in russo il suo libro Lo potevo fare anch’io! , dedicato alla comprensione dell’arte contemporanea e alle difficoltà che spesso accompagnano il rapporto tra opere e spettatori. Nel 2024, poi, Bonami ha curato con Zelfira Tregulova Square and Space. From Malevich to GES-2 , progetto che ha messo in relazione l’eredità dell’avanguardia con la storia e l’identità dell’istituzione moscovita.

In quell’occasione, Bonami ha affermato: «Il mio rapporto di collaborazione e amicizia con la V-A-C Foundation va avanti dal 2008, da 16 anni, e non si è mai interrotto. Non sono stato “attirato” quindi e non da Mosca ma da un progetto culturale che rimane una delle poche zone di speranza. Ges2 disegnata da Renzo Piano e Rpbw è un luogo vitale visitato dalla sua apertura da più di un milione di persone che al suo interno trovano una tranquillità e un’offerta culturale eccezionali. Distruggere o interrompere il dialogo e lo scambio culturale significa da sempre abbandonare ogni speranza di pace. Da curatore sento la responsabilità verso le giovani generazioni di mantenere questo dialogo aperto, non importa il rischio che posso correre, sia professionale che personale. La mia non è una decisione ma banalmente un obbligo intellettuale. La mostra sarà un grande riflessione sulla trasformazione del rapporto fra opera d’arte, architettura e spazio sociale. Dal gesto radicale alla cultura dei selfie».

GES-2 House of Culture, da centrale elettrica a centro culturale

GES-2 ha aperto al pubblico il 4 dicembre 2021 negli spazi di una ex centrale elettrica dei primi del Novecento situata sull’argine di Bolotnaya, nel centro di Mosca, proprio di fronte al Cremlino, un edificio trasformato su progetto dello studio di Renzo Piano in un centro dedicato alla produzione e alla diffusione della cultura contemporanea. La denominazione “House of Culture” richiama il modello delle “case della cultura”, luoghi storicamente destinati ad accogliere attività artistiche, formative, teatrali e cinematografiche della vecchia Unione Sovietica. GES-2 ne propone una reinterpretazione in chiave contemporanea, con una programmazione che ne mantiene la multidisciplinarietà mettendo in relazione arti visive, performance, musica, attività laboratoriali e iniziative rivolte al pubblico.

La V-A-C Foundation

Lo spazio è stato sviluppato dalla V-A-C Foundation, fondata a Mosca nel 2009 da Leonid Mikhelson , imprenditore attivo nel settore energetico e a capo di Novatek, tra i principali produttori di gas naturale in Russia. La Fondazione ha promosso progetti dedicati alla sperimentazione artistica e alla diffusione della cultura contemporanea, sviluppando attività anche fuori dal Paese, tra cui quelle ospitate a Palazzo Zattere, a Venezia. Il profilo del suo fondatore, però, introduce una questione che riguarda il rapporto tra finanziamenti privati e autonomia culturale: Mikhelson è infatti un magnate del gas, una figura di primo piano dell’economia russa ed è considerato vicino al presidente Vladimir Putin . La dimensione privata della fondazione non la rende estranea al contesto economico e politico in cui opera; al contrario, le risorse che sostengono il progetto culturale provengono da un’attività strettamente legata a un settore strategico per l’economia russa.

Nel 2022, l’allora direttore artistico della Fondazione, Francesco Manacorda , lasciò l’incarico a causa dell’invasione russa dell’Ucraina, mentre le attività della sede veneziana di Palazzo Zattere furono sospese. GES-2, invece, ha continuato a operare a Mosca.

Poco dopo l’inizio della guerra, anche l’artista islandese Ragnar Kjartansson annullò le performance previste a GES-2, dichiarando: «Non è possibile presentare questo lavoro mentre comincia l’orrore».

La nuova direzione e i prossimi progetti

Nel nuovo ruolo, Bonami lavorerà con il gruppo curatoriale alla selezione e allo sviluppo dei progetti, contribuendo a dare continuità al programma già avviato. Tra i progetti già annunciati figura Things, Idols, Bananas , previsto per dicembre 2026 e curato da Bonami insieme a Dmitry Belkin . Le linee tematiche e i progetti per il prossimo triennio saranno presentati entro la fine dell’anno, e la nuova direzione dovrà confrontarsi con un programma in evoluzione, che mantenga il rapporto tra produzione e ricerca artistica, insieme a un’apertura a linguaggi differenti che caratterizza l’identità dichiarata del centro.

Dopo il febbraio 2022, la possibilità di collaborare con istituzioni russe è diventata oggetto di un confronto che coinvolge artisti, curatori, musei e organizzatori di eventi. Resta da vedere come le scelte artistiche del prossimo triennio si misureranno con il contesto in cui il centro opera e quale spazio sarà possibile riservare alla dimensione internazionale del progetto. E se quello del delicato rapporto con la Russia è un tema che ha attraversato l’edizione della Biennale di quest’anno e ha infuocato manifestazioni e proteste , la nomina di Bonami riapre con forza questo capitolo e continua a interrogare il sistema dell’arte su quanto – e su come – un progetto culturale possa dirsi davvero indipendente rispetto a strutture economiche e politiche che lo rendono possibile.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Talia Ryder ( Never Rarely Sometimes Always ) is set for a third lead role opposite Kit Connor and Diana Silvers in PRƎPPY , the true-crime flick from STX Entertainment and Aggregate Films that we recently scooped . Also newly aboard the film, helmed by Janicza Bravo, are Presumed Innocent ‘s Elizabeth Marvel and Bill Camp .

Character details are being kept under wraps, other than the fact that Marvel and Camp — a pair of decorated, married actors — will portray a married couple. Production is now underway in Manhattan.

Based on an original screenplay by David Levine and Rose Lichter-Marck, PRƎPPY explores the summer of 1986 leading to the murder of recent high school graduate Jennifer Levin at the hands of Robert Chambers, a former Manhattan private-school student, in New York’s Central Park. The shocking crime — in which Chambers was dubbed the “Preppy Killer” — captivated a generation and put privilege, class and sex on trial.

Kit Connor & Diana Silvers To Star In "Preppy Killer" Pic 'PRƎPPY' For STX, Aggregate; Janicza Bravo Directing

Jason Bateman, Michael Costigan and John Buderwitz are producing for Aggregate, alongside Peter Coleman and Paula Manzanedo for STX, and Bravo.

Best known for her breakout performance in Eliza Hittman’s Focus drama Never Rarely Sometimes Always , which brought her both an Independent Spirit Award and a Critics’ Choice Award nomination, Ryder most recently wrapped a lead role opposite Mark Eydelshteyn in the second season of Prime Video’s Mr. & Mrs. Smith . Before that, she and Michael Shannon wrapped on a contemporary reimagining of horror classic The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari . Ryder just signed on for a role opposite Tom Holland in his Fred Astaire biopic for Sony. Her films next up for release are Frankie Shaw’s 4 Kids Walk Into a Bank and Rob Burnett’s In Memoriam . She is represented by LBI Entertainment, UTA, and Vainshtein Law, P.C.

Coming off roles in Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day and Apple’s acclaimed legal thriller Presumed Innocent , Marvel is repped by Verve, Viking Entertainment, and Franklin, Weinrib, Rudell & Vassallo.

A Tony, two-time Emmy and SAG Award nominee, Camp co-starred opposite Marvel in Presumed Innocent ‘s first season. Next up, he returns to Apple with a role opposite Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, and Stephen Graham in Nocturne , a crime thriller series premiering October 30. He is repped by UTA and Franklin, Weinrib, Rudell & Vassallo, P.C.

article_text:
Zum Welttag des audiovisuellen Erbes am 27. Oktober 2026 finden rund 40 Events in der ganzen Schweiz zu den verschiedensten Interessensbereichen statt, darunter ?? Veranstaltungen zu fotografischen Themen. Einige davon sind noch über einen längeren Zeitraum zu besuchen.

«Weisch no?» Die Schweiz feiert ihr audiovisuelles Erbe. Von der Suche nach der ältesten Fotografie der Schweiz über die Wiederaufführung von Ernst A. Heinigers 360°-Film bis hin zu einem Konzertabend, der Yehudi Menuhins «Lost Tapes» seltener Konzertaufnahmen aus den 1970er-Jahren mit einem Live-Konzert kombiniert: Rund um den 27. Oktober 2026 rückt der Welttag des audiovisuellen Erbes die Bedeutung von Bild- und Tondokumenten für das audiovisuelle Gedächtnis der Schweiz ins Zentrum. 40 Veranstaltungen in allen vier Sprachregionen laden dazu ein, dieses vielfältige Kulturerbe neu zu entdecken.

In unserem Artikel führen wir die Events und Veranstaltungen zu fotografischen Themen auf, die heute und über einen längeren Zeitraum stattfinenden.

Memoriav suchte die älteste Fotografie der Schweiz

Dieses Jahr feiert die Fotografie ihr 200-jähriges Bestehen. Dazu lanciert Memoriav zum Welttag des audiovisuellen Erbes am 27. Oktober eine Challenge durch die Schweizer Fotosammlungen. Die Challenge-Frage: Welche ist die älteste Fotografie, die in einer Gedächtnisinstitution in der Schweiz aufbewahrt wird? Sammler und Institutionen haben 27 Tage Zeit, um in ihren Fotosammlungen und Fotobeständen nach zwei besonderen fotografischen Objekten zu suchen: • der ältesten Fotografie einer Schweizer Landschaft oder eines Schweizer Gebäudes • das älteste in der Schweiz aufgenommene fotografische Porträt Man darf gespannt sein, welche fotografischen Ikonen dabei zutage kommen.

Basel: Van Gogh, Hodler und ein Cabriolet (Sammlung Gertrud Dübi-Müller)

Gertrud Dübi-Müller war eine der bedeutendsten Kunstsammler/innen der Schweiz, passionierte Fotografin, Autofahrerin, Bergsteigerin, und sie stand Modell für Ferdinand Hodler und andere Kunstschaffende. Das Kunstmuseum Basel zeigt mit Van Gogh, Hodler und ein Cabriolet die erste umfassende Ausstellung über Gertrud Dübi-Müller (1888, Solothurn–1980, Solothurn). In der Ausstellung sind auch Fotografien von Gertrud Dübi-Müller aus der Sammlung der Fotostiftung Schweiz zu sehen, die mit der Unterstützung von Memoriav erhalten wurden.

Kunstmuseum Basel, 19. September 2026 – 7. Februar 2027, Infos

Basel: Das PIA-Projekt: Participatory Knowledge Practices in Analogue and Digital Image Archives

Anlässlich des Welttags des audiovisuellen Erbes lädt das Archiv der Empirischen Kulturwissenschaft Schweiz (EKWS) zu einer Präsentation des zwischen 2021 und 2025 durchgeführten SNF-Projektes «Participatory Knowledge Practices in Analogue and Digital Image Archives» (PIA) ein. In diesem Rahmen wurden drei fotografische Bestände des EKWS-Fotoarchivs mit Unterstützung von Memoriav restauriert, digitalisiert und erschlossen. Im Zentrum des Interesses standen die Transformation der Bestände von der analogen zur digitalen Welt und die Bedingungen, die ein Archiv zu einem lebendigen Ort der Wissensgenerierung, der Wissensspeicherung und der Wissensvermittlung machen.

Eikones Forum, Rheinsprung 11, 4051 Basel, 27. – 28. Oktober 2026. Infos

Lausanne: «Photo-sensible»: Die Glasnegative von André Schmid

Das Historische Museum von Lausanne (MHL) präsentiert «Photo-sensible», eine Ausstellung, die den Glasnegativen des Lausanner Fotografen André Schmid gewidmet ist. Als beeindruckendes Zeugnis des fotografischen Schaffens vom Ende des 19. und Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts faszinieren diese Negative sowohl durch ihren dokumentarischen Wert als auch durch ihre ästhetische Qualität. In einer Inszenierung, die ihr ausdrucksstarkes und zeitloses Potenzial hervorhebt, erinnert die Ausstellung daran, dass das fotografische Bild ursprünglich auch ein materielles Objekt ist.

Musée historique de Lausanne, Place de la Cathédrale 4, 1005 Lausanne, 10. September 2026 – 14. März 2027. Infos

Le Locle: «Die ersten Fotografien. Bis zum Beweis des Gegenteils»

Was macht ein Foto zu einer «Ersten»? Wie lässt sich beweisen, dass es tatsächlich die erste ist? Und was passiert, wenn neue Forschungsergebnisse eine Geschichte in Frage stellen, die man für feststehend hielt? Anlässlich des 200-jährigen Jubiläums der Fotografie lädt das Musée des Beaux-Arts Le Locle (MBAL) mit der Ausstellung «Les premières photographies. Jusqu’à preuve du contraire», kuratiert von Francesca Seravalle, vom dazu ein, sich auf die Suche nach diesen wegweisenden Bildern zu begeben.

Musée des Beaux-Arts Le Locle (MBAL), Rue Marie-Anne-Calame 6, 2400 Le Locle. 27. Oktober 2026 bis 21. Februar 2027. Infos

Die Auswahl umfasst Aufzeichnungen von Debatten des Stadtrats zum Cornaredo-Stadion sowie Fotografien aus dem Fotobestand von Vincenzo Vicari, der im Historischen Archiv der Stadt Lugano aufbewahrt wird.

Die der Initiative gewidmete Webseite ist ab sofort hier online verfügbar .

Luzern: Ausstellung «Stil und Zeit – Der Fotograf Hans Eggermann»

Anlässlich des Welttags des audiovisuellen Erbes präsentiert das Staatsarchiv Luzern eine Ausstellung mit Fotografien aus dem Vorlass des Luzerner Fotografen Hans Eggermann. Im Mittelpunkt stehen Aufnahmen zu Mode und Design der 1960er- und 1970er-Jahre, zwei Themenbereiche, die Eggermanns fotografische Arbeit in den ersten Jahrzehnten seiner Selbstständigkeit prägten. Ergänzt wird die Auswahl durch eine Bilddokumentation seiner Arbeitsbiografie bis 2014. Zu sehen sind zudem die digitalisierte Tonbildschau «Es gehört zum guten Ton … – John Lay Electronics», Littau-Luzern (1986) sowie das Video «Der Konzertsaal, Stille – Klang – Echo» über das Luzerner Kunst- und Kongresshaus KKL aus dem Jahr 1999.

Payerne: Fotografien der Schweizer Luftwaffe, 1985–1995

Anlässlich des Welttags des audiovisuellen Kulturerbes bietet der Verein Cibachrome (Freiburg) anhand einer umfangreichen Auswahl an Fotodokumenten einen Einblick in die jüngste Geschichte der Schweizer Luftwaffe. Fotografien von Flugzeugen im Flug oder am Boden, Szenen aus dem Luftfahrtbetrieb und Dokumente, die von einer besonderen Epoche in der Geschichte der Schweizer Militärluftfahrt zeugen: Diese Ausstellung ermöglicht es, diese Bilder als Fragmente eines heute wertvollen visuellen Gedächtnisses neu zu entdecken. Diese vom Verein Cibachrome in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Musée Clin d’Ailes organisierte Veranstaltung verbindet somit die Entdeckung des fotografischen Erbes mit der Erkundung eines symbolträchtigen Ortes der Schweizer Luftfahrtgeschichte.

Sursee: Foto Friebel – Visuelles Kulturerbe als Werkzeug der Denkmalpflege

Fast hundert Jahre lang war Foto Friebel in Sursee tätig. Das umfangreiche Archiv mit rund 700’000 Fotografien wird heute vom Stadtarchiv Sursee und von der Fachstelle audiovisuelles Kulturgut (FAV) der ZHB Luzern verwaltet, aufbereitet und der Öffentlichkeit zugänglich gemacht. Welchen dokumentarischen Wert hat ein solches Bildarchiv für die Denkmalpflege, die Stadtentwicklung oder die Dokumentation von Baukultur? Und welchen Wert hat es für die Archive, die es der Öffentlichkeit zugänglich machen? Diesen Fragen geht die FAV am UNESCO-Welttag des audiovisuellen Kulturerbes nach. Mit der Stadtarchivarin Nicole Bättig und Marcus Casutt von der Denkmalpflege Kanton Luzern bespricht Simon Meyer, Leiter der FAV, Fotografien aus dem Bestand Friebel und ihre Bedeutung als visuelles Erbe.

Pfarreizentrum Sursee, St. Urbanstrasse 8, 6210 Sursee, Dienstag, 27. Oktober 2026, 19.30 bis 20.30 Uhr. Infos . Download: Welttag 2026 – Flyer Foto Friebel Sursee ( PDF)

Eine praktische Erfahrung, die auch dazu anregt, über das Verhältnis zwischen Fotografie und Realität nachzudenken: Sagt ein Foto immer die Wahrheit?

Memoriav Workshop: Notfallmassnahmen bei Fotosammlungen: Risiken vorbeugen und eingreifen

Was tun, wenn eine Fotosammlung von einem Schadensfall bedroht ist? Wie lassen sich Schäden begrenzen und wie kann man schnell handeln, um teilweise unersetzliche Bilder zu retten? Dieser Kurs bietet eine praktische Einführung in die Schadensprävention und die ersten Massnahmen zur Rettung von Fotografien. Anhand von theoretischen Beiträgen und Workshops lernen die Teilnehmenden, wie sie Risiken erkennen, einen Präventionsplan erstellen und in Notfällen wirksam handeln können. Der Workshop ist ausgebucht, es gibt aber eine Warteliste.

Memoriav, Sulgenrain 20, 3007 Bern, 30. Oktober 2026, 90:30-16:30 Uhr . Infos . Anmeldung .

article_text:
The “Baby Holga” Project

© Alec Pain (@alecpain) , England, United Kingdom

Last summer, a random comment I made on an image in a Facebook Holga group led me to a new acquaintance, Alec Pain , who runs The Daily Holga feed on Instagram. That opened a door to me to an invitation to participate in a then-newly-formed project where participants from the United States would use borrowed Baby Holga cameras sent by mail between participants to make images.

I found the project interesting from the outset enough that I knew I wanted to interview Alec about it. Several months in, we get to see how it was originally conceived, how it evolved, and what he foresees for the future of the project. I hope you find this as interesting as I did.

© Alec Pain (@alecpain) , England, United Kingdom

DNJ: Tell us a little about your own photographic practice and your interest in Holga cameras.

AP: I guess I’m an experimental film photographer who sometimes calls myself an artist, but I love taking photos of anything, with anything, whether that be a Holga, a digital camera, or an iPhone.

I’m really interested in Holga cameras. I’m something of a hoarder: I have been trying to collect the different Holgas that have come out over the years – from all of the different Holga letters – Holga N, to GN, FN, CFN, GFN, GCFN, etc through to the 135 makes, the 3D ones, the digital ones. Anything that has a Holga (and Woca) written on it! I now have 54 different makes, but two are still missing from my list (plus new ones that appear and surprise me!). The two I am missing are the WOCA NF-4 and the Holga 135T—if anyone has them!

I run a feed on Instagram called The Daily Holga, which means I post pretty much every day. That might change to the Weekly Holga at some point. I’ve been posting since 2023; I put up challenges, themes, monthly “artists in residence” who showcase their work, and the odd competition.

There’s an annual competition called Noddy Holga where I do a backward advent calendar. You enter the competition, then a judging panel chooses their top ten favorite images and ranks each selection from one to ten. The competition winner is the image that garnered the most points. It sounds complex, but it’s straightforward. I think it’s fairer than a people’s-choice vote, which usually ends up decided by whoever has the most friends who voted. It’s then announced daily by counting down from 24 to the winner, who is announced on Christmas Eve on both Noddy Holga and The Daily Holga.

© Alec Pain (@alecpain) , England, United Kingdom

DNJ: What initially drew you to the “Baby Holga” camera?

AP: I’m a collector of Holgas, so what initially drew me to the Baby Holga was that it is a Holga. That said, I loved the fact that it was a keychain/keyring size – something you could fit in your pocket. More recently, when Kodak brought out their Charmera digital camera, Holga followed suit with a digital keychain Holga—which looked like the original Baby Holga. I thought: “Why isn’t there a keychain camera in use that is analogue?”

I owned two “Baby Holgas” – they were originally called Micro 110 Holgas. Holga made them originally; Superheadz in Japan repackaged them as Baby Holgas. They also produced a “Daddy/Mummy” and “Baby” Holga set called Oyakö. They aren’t made anymore, but I managed to find some on buyee.com. One of the participants (@fromdalens) lives in Hong Kong and found some too.

Creatively, I liked the challenge of making art with something so small and basic. I also loved the way you got most of the image ghosting onto the edges of the film.

© Andy Swart (@holga_aquarium) , Minnesota, United States

© @_thedecisivemoment , Massachusetts, United States

DNJ: How did the idea for The Baby Holga Project come about? Was there a particular moment when you realized you wanted to send these tiny cameras around the world?

AP: I’d been in contact with Holga about remaking the cameras because they were out of production, and I wanted to make a Daily Holga edition. Then I realized they’d be the perfect camera to use for a continuous camera swap via mail. They’re small, easy to use, and relatively inexpensive to send on to the next person. I was going to start with just one Baby Holga traveling the globe; I’d asked Lisa Tang Liu if she’d be interested in starting it off. I then met Kelly Ann Gray at Photo London and passed her the first Baby Holga; after she worked with it, she sent it to Lisa.

© Lisa Tang Liu (@expert.in.nothing), Massachusetts, United States

© Kelly Ann Gray (@kellyanngray) , New York, United States

DNJ: Can you walk us through how the project works, from the moment someone receives a camera to when they pass it along? Are there any guidelines for what participants photograph, or is that entirely up to them?

AP: I’ve tried to make it as simple as possible. The costs are minimal: film, development, and one-way postage. The challenge is the same for every photographer: 24 exposures with 110 film using a very limited camera. The only difference will be the choice of film. The camera is borrowed at no cost; each photographer purchases and develops their own film. Once a photographer receives the camera, they have two to three weeks to shoot a roll of 110 film with the camera. Most people buy two rolls as it takes time to get used to the “rangefinder”, and it can have a fairly low success rate! We stipulate that each participant shoots, develops, and then scans one roll of film before sending it on to the next person. I receive the scans of images and publish them on both the Baby Holga and The Daily Holga feeds on Instagram. The copyright remains with the photographers. We hope then to create a book and an exhibition with the images.

Maureen Bond had entered some images for Holga Week and owned her own, so she sent me the first scans and kicked the project off along with Lisa and Kelly Ann.

Casey Davis also made a spreadsheet to help with that process.

© Maureen Bond (@maureenbond) , California, United States

© Paulina Mannisto (@analogue.flaneuring) , Finland

DNJ: Were you looking for photographers who already work with toy cameras and alternative processes, or were you interested in seeing what artists from very different photographic backgrounds might do with the Baby Holga? Has this changed or evolved over the months this project has been going on?

AP: I started with photographers and artists I already knew – and mainly it’s been drawn from followers of The Daily Holga, but I’ve had people contact me who I don’t know and are keen to be part of the swap. Lisa came up with the fantastic idea of covering all 50 US states – and we have 49 of them – with South Carolina being the only state we are missing! I wanted it to be global, and so we now have 20 cameras circling the world. Six in the U.S., five in Europe, four in the UK, one in Canada, one in Mexico, one in South America, one in Asia, and one in Australasia.

© Kristi Cornell (@kccornell) , Louisiana, USA

© Christian J (@am_wegrand_fotografie) , Germany

DNJ: The Baby Holga is an extraordinarily simple camera, with very little control over the final image. What do you think happens creatively when photographers are handed something so basic?

AP: I think that, like me, they’ll still be able to create fantastic images and are sometimes rudely awakened by the camera’s shortcomings!

© Rachel (@vivid_opia), England, United Kingdom

© Jim Martin (@lofijim) , England, United Kingdom

DNJ: You’ve assembled quite an international group of participants. How did you find the photographers? What has the response been like? Were there any places that were particularly difficult to reach?

AP: The original target was for 110 photographers on 110 film, but we’ve surpassed that. I’m hopeful the project can keep going much longer, with a lot more participants. California has had the most responses. Most have been found because they followed the Daily Holga. In the US, we’ve found the rest through word of mouth or by searching the internet for those missing States. I think we are up to nearly 200 people involved at this point.

DNJ: You’ve essentially created a network of photographers connected by a tiny plastic camera. Has the project developed in ways you didn’t anticipate once those cameras began traveling?

AP: The project evolved from one camera sent around the world over a long period, between people I knew or wanted to work with, to twenty cameras and many requests through Instagram. I did think it had legs – that it was a fun way of bringing the film community together to create something bigger. I was surprised to see so many people interested in being part of the project.

© Jamison Davis (@likethe.whiskey) , Alaska, USA

© Emma Ledwith (@emledportraits) , England, United Kingdom

DNJ: There is a certain amount of trust involved in sending cameras around the world, often between people who have never met. Have there been any unexpected experiences, mishaps, or particularly memorable stories along the way?

AP: Because it’s such a small camera, we’ve been lucky (so far!) that nobody has decided to keep the camera.

© holgaforever , Canada

© Claire Grant x Lee Wilkes (@grantxwilkes) , Australia

DNJ: As images begin coming in from different countries, are you seeing any common threads in how people approach the camera, or has the work been as varied as the photographers themselves? Has anything surprised you?

AP: It’s been interesting to see how different photographers have handled the Baby Holga’s lack of control and still created beautiful images.

© Maximiliano Vernazza (@maxivernazza) , Argentina

© Anna Starr (@anna.s.snapshots) , Washington, USA

DNJ: What, if anything, have you discovered about the photographic community through this project that you might not have discovered otherwise?

AP: So far, that it is a wonderful community—one that is both generous and engaged.

DNJ: One of your goals is to persuade Holga to bring back the Baby Holga. Have you had any conversations with the manufacturer about the possibility?

AP: I’m in discussions with the people who make Holga cameras. To make this happen, I need to raise enough money to make 2,000 Baby Holgas. It’s going to be tricky, but I’m looking into Kickstarter (or something similar) to reach an amount where I can guarantee I won’t be out of pocket. I’d likely sell the camera for around $20-25. I think if I can get to 1,000 buyers, I should be able to go ahead, but I’m still working out the exact numbers.

@ Jennifer H (@jensfineart) , Canada

© Tagen Towsley Baker (@tagentbaker) , Idaho & Virginia, United States

DNJ: You’re also planning a book documenting the project. How do you envision bringing together photographs made by so many different people, in so many different places, into a cohesive publication?

AP: There would be two books: one US-only, comprising the photographers from the 50 states (and possibly Washington, DC); and one with the rest of the global participants. I’ve preliminarily titled the books Baby, I Love You—110 Photographers Using 110 Film .

The general idea is to have one page per person, with their name, IG tag, a short bio, and a map detailing their location, with one image, possibly one or two more.

© Erin Mussett (@erinon.film) , Florida, United States

© Manu Solian (@manuomanolo) , Argentina

DNJ: Beyond the photographs and the possibility of bringing back the camera, what do you hope people will take away from The Baby Holga Project?

AP: I’m most interested in people learning and taking inspiration from what’s around them—from both the old and new—whether that’s a £5k digital camera, a £20 tiny plastic camera, or, conversely and a little hesitantly, something like AI.

I hope viewers take away a few things: first, that you can make beautiful images with a tiny key ring camera; second, that the images will inspire them to make their own images; third, that they might swap cameras or work with others to learn new things.

For the participants, that they’ve been part of a community and taken some images they are proud of.

© Pasán Pelís (@naudi.cfn) , Argentina

DNJ: Thank you, so much Alec, for giving us such a broad window into this fascinating project. I cannot wait to see more work from the participants as the project keeps evolving.

© Mateo (@latitudeslongitudes) , Washington, United States

article_text:
A wholly modern horror story is set to get the feature treatment.

“ iHunt: Killing Monsters in the Gig Economy ,” the independently distributed novel series and tabletop RPG by Hill and Young, is getting a film adaptation.

Olivia Hill wrote the script. Hill and Young are a Chicago-based queer married writing duo who have developed the “iHunt” universe over seven novels released during 10 years under their Machine Age Productions banner. Hill is a trans woman, and the project is LGBTQIA+-led.

Related Stories

Harry Styles 'Together, Together' Tour Doc Coming From John Wilson, Universal Pictures Content Group (EXCLUSIVE)

Harry Styles Debuts Unreleased Song He Wrote in Memory of Liam Payne, 'What Is Enough,' on Second Anniversary of Ex-Bandmate's Death

Scott Glosserman, who helmed both “Behind the Mask: The Rise of Leslie Vernon” and its currently-in-production sequel , is set to direct. Jess Elgene is featured as Sandra, a new character created for the film. The project will be filmed in association with Anarchists United Studios, with Lilly Wachowski (“The Matrix”), Sarah Marie Flores and Lawrence Mattis set as executive producers. The feature is also produced by Matt Skrobalak (Butler Hall Productions), Stirling Matheson (Bravura Arts and Entertainment Ltd.) and Hill and Filamena Young (Machine Age Productions).

Per the official synopsis, “Set in the fictional California city of San Jenaro, #iHunt follows a trio of women who are best friends navigating monster-hunting through a gig-work app, blending horror-comedy with sharp socioeconomic commentary.”

“#iHunt has been our focus for the past 10 years, and we want nothing more than to bring it to a wider audience,” Hill and Young said in a statement. “Supernatural horror has always been an amazing tool for telling stories about the very real problems people face. And if you’ve stood up to eviction and Dracula, you know eviction can be so much scarier.”

“What drew me to Olivia’s script is how cleverly she uses the conventions of horror to explore something genuinely frightening, which is the illusion of choice in a world where survival itself has become a gig. It’s irreverent, provocative and supremely entertaining, but beneath all the monsters and mayhem is a story about what freedom really means when you can’t afford to say no. That’s the kind of genre storytelling I love,” Glosserman also said in a statement.

“Anarchists United is thrilled to be on board with #iHunt and support Olivia Hill and Filamena Young’s referential and all too relatable world of late late-stage capitalism in the vampiric age,” Anarchists United said in a statement. “Even in afterdeath, access to health insurance bites, but besties are worth fighting for.”

In addition to the movie, a TV pilot written by Hill and Young is also in development, with Anne Cofell Saunders (“The Boys”) attached as showrunner.

Per the pilot’s logline, “Set in the same city with an entirely different cast of characters, the pilot follows Lana, who leads a crew of broke hunters taking gigs through the app until a routine hospital job turns into a full-blown monster infestation and puts them on the radar of Arthur, an ancient vampire executive.”

Hill and Young have also created “#iHunt: A Night in the Life,” a vertical series in which, per the logline, “Hannah, a struggling hunter, figures out the real money is in content and starts livestreaming her monster hunts.”

Elgene is represented by Artists First and Resolute Artists Agency. Glosserman is represented by attorney Tanya Mallean of Skrzyniarz & Mallean. Matheson is represented by attorney Arthur Evrensel of MEP Business Counsel.

See the key art for the project below.

11月3日「文化の日」は「自由と平和を愛し、文化をすすめる」ことを趣旨に、1948年に制定された国民の祝日。国内の美術館や博物館、文化施設の一部では、コレクション展や常設展を中心に入場料が無料になる。本記事では、そのなかから12館をピックアップ。この機会に、これまで訪れたことのない文化施設を巡ってみるのはいかがだろうか。

【東京】 東京国立博物館

「東博コレクション展」

上野・東京国立博物館では、東博コレクション展（平常展）観覧料が無料になる（通常一般1000円）。東博コレクション展とは、本館、東洋館、平成館考古展示室、法隆寺宝物館、黒田記念館の5つの展示館で見られる平常展の総称。東博のコレクションは国宝90件、重要文化財652件（2026年4月現在）を含む12万件以上の所蔵品と、個人や社寺等から寄託品として預かっている多数の貴重な文化財から構成されており、東博コレクション展では常時3000件以上の作品を展示している。11月3日には平成館 企画展示室にて「渡来人が見た長野―馬と歩んだ古墳時代―」の特集展示も行われ、こちらも無料で観覧できる。

【東京】 国立西洋美術館

「国立西洋美術館 常設展」

松方コレクションをその軸として1959年に開館した国立西洋美術館では、常設展の観覧料が無料になる（通常一般500円）。常設展では、中世末期から20世紀初頭にかけての西洋絵画と、ロダンを中心とするフランス近代彫刻を本館、新館、前庭で年間を通じて展示している。11月3日には小企画展「劇場をめぐるイメージ―ドラクロワ、ドーミエからトゥールーズ=ロートレック、クリンガーまで」と特集展示「「昭和100年」 昭和時代 当館における保存修復の変遷」も行われており、こちらも無料で観覧できる。

【東京】 国立科学博物館

「常設展示」

日本でもっとも歴史のある博物館のひとつであり、国立で唯一の総合科学博物館である同館では、常設展示が無料で公開される（通常一般630円）。日本列島をテーマにした「日本館」と、地球生命史や科学技術をテーマにした「地球館」のふたつの館で行われるコレクション展示のほか、「野口英世生誕150年記念企画展『感染症への挑戦：過去・現在・未来』」も無料で観覧可能だ。

【東京】 東京国立近代美術館

「MOMATコレクション」「あみ・ど・ぱり 巴里の日本人芸術家たち」

1952年に誕生した日本で最初の国立美術館である国立近代美術館では、「所蔵作品展 MOMATコレクション」とコレクションによる小企画「あみ・ど・ぱり 巴里の日本人芸術家たち」の観覧料が無料になる（通常一般500円）。MOMATコレクションは、1952年の開館以来の活動を通じて収集してきた1万4000点を超える所蔵作品から、会期ごとに約200点を展示する国内最大級のコレクション展。小企画の「あみ・ど・ぱり」とは、パリに滞在経験のある芸術家、作家、実業家らによって1930年に結成された社交団体、巴里会の機関誌のタイトルのことで、戦前から戦後にかけてパリに渡って研鑽を積み、サロンなどで活躍した日本人芸術家たちを紹介する。

【東京】 国立映画アーカイブ

「NFAJコレクションでみる 日本映画の歴史」「没後70年 映画監督 溝口健二」

日本で唯一の国立映画機関、国立映画アーカイブでは、常設展「NFAJコレクションでみる 日本映画の歴史」のほか没後70年の節目として開催される溝口健二（1898〜1956）初の本格的回顧展「没後70年 映画監督 溝口健二」が無料で公開される（通常一般600円）。常設展では、映画の渡来した19世紀末から発展を続けた日本映画の歴史を、多彩なコレクション（ポスター・スチル写真・雑誌・製作資料・業界資料・キャメラなど機械類・映画人の遺品・映像など）によってたどる。企画展では、『西鶴一代女』、『雨月物語』、『山椒大夫』などで知られる溝口の濃密な映画芸術に迫る。

【栃木】 栃木県立美術館

「松本哲男展」

栃木県を中心とする国内の近現代美術や、フランス、イギリス、ドイツなど西欧の近現代美術作品をコレクションの要とする栃木県立美術館では、「栃木×工芸 －技と美の出会い」「柄澤齊の迷宮」をテーマとするコレクション展のほか、企画展「松本哲男展」が無料公開の対象となる（通常一般1250円）。松本哲男（1943〜2012）は、栃木県佐野市に生まれ、世界各地の景勝地を大画面に描き続けた日本画家。栃木県内の自然風景を描いていた初期の作品から、晩年の大型作品までを展示する。

【神奈川】 横須賀美術館

「令和8年度第1期所蔵品展」「丸山純子 呼吸する庭」

2026年9月にリニューアルオープンした横須賀美術館では、「令和8年度第1期所蔵品展」の観覧料が無料になる（通常一般450円）。再オープンを記念した今会期は、近年購入、寄贈によって収蔵した作品によって構成される。また、所蔵品展の特集「丸山純子 呼吸する庭」も合わせて鑑賞できる。横須賀に在住し、身の回りの素材を用いながら「再生」や「循環」をテーマに制作を続ける丸山のインスタレーションが展示される。

【神奈川】 神奈川県立近代美術館 葉山

「銅版画家・駒井哲郎 掌上にひろがる星座のように」

神奈川県立近代美術館 葉山では、日本の版画史に重要な足跡をのこした、銅版画家・駒井哲郎（1920〜1976）の初期から晩年までの軌跡をたどる「銅版画家・駒井哲郎 掌上にひろがる星座のように」が無料公開の対象となる（通常一般1200円）。世田谷美術館の福原義春コレクションを主軸に、駒井が影響を受けたオディロン・ルドンや長谷川潔、恩地孝四郎といった国内外の作家の作品に加え、銅原版、制作道具、写真などを通し、多岐にわたる創作活動と、その人間像に迫る。同時開催のコレクション展「たそかれ、かはたれ ―現代美術における“翳”」も合わせて鑑賞しよう。

【石川】 国立工芸館

「デザイン・クロニクル展 なにが生まれて、なにが変わった？」

工芸とデザインを専門的に扱う国内で唯一の美術館、国立工芸館では、デザインの歴史を総合的に紹介する金沢移転後初の展覧会「デザイン・クロニクル展 なにが生まれて、なにが変わった？」の観覧料が無料になる（通常一般1200円）。国立工芸館のデザインコレクションを中心に紹介し、19世紀後半のアーツ＆クラフツ運動からアール・ヌーヴォーとアール・デコ、そしてバウハウスに代表されるモダニズム・デザイン、さらに第二次大戦後の展開までの100年あまりのデザインの流れをたどる。

【大阪】 国立国際美術館

「開館50周年記念プレ企画 コレクション1：私／行為」

2027年に開館50周年を迎える国立国際美術館では、そのプレ企画として「開館50周年記念プレ企画 コレクション1：私／行為」が開催されており、無料公開の対象となる（通常一般430円）。コレクション1では、同館のコレクションでも最も古い1890年代制作のポール・セザンヌの作品から、1960年代半ばまでの作品を紹介し、この時代の美術における制作の主体としての「私」の確立と揺らぎ、そして制作「行為」の在り方とそれをめぐる言説の変容に注目する。

【兵庫】 兵庫県立美術館

「前衛ってなんだ？」「美術の中のかたち―手で見る造形 青木野枝 動体」

兵庫県立美術館では、コレクション展が無料で公開される（通常一般550円）。「前衛ってなんだ？」は、1986年パリのポンピドゥー・センターで開かれ、日本近現代美術の再評価のきっかけとなった「前衛芸術の日本 1910‒1970」展をきっかけに、「前衛」をいまいちど振り返るコレクション展。同会期には、彫刻家・青木野枝（1958〜）を迎えた、見ること、触れることを探る小企画「美術の中のかたち―手で見る造形 青木野枝 動体」も開催されている。

【広島】 広島市現代美術館

「千崎千恵夫 眼差しの奥にむかって」

広島市現代美術館では10月24日から始まる「千崎千恵夫 眼差しの奥にむかって」が無料公開の対象となる（通常一般1100円）。本展は、広島県呉市出身のアーティスト・千崎千恵夫（1953〜）の1990年以降に制作された作品を中心に、最新作を含む約100点で構成される。「自然と人工」をテーマに、様々なメディアを駆使した制作を通して人間存在と世界の在り方を探求してきた千崎が見出した世界の姿とは。「時間の束」をテーマとした「コレクション展2026-Ⅱ」も一緒に鑑賞できる。

Estrenos Apple TV – Películas y series nuevas del 26 al 30 de octubre 2026

Staff Cine PREMIERE

¿Qué verás este mes?

Conoce aquí todos los estrenos de películas y series nuevas que llegan a Apple TV en octubre 2026. Es cierto que la plataforma de streaming de la manzanita no estrena tantas series y películas como otros sistemas, pero la calidad de cada uno de sus títulos justifican esta aparente austeridad de novedades. Aún así, una de las grandes ventajas de Apple TV es la facilidad que provee para rentar y comprar títulos de manera independiente aunque no sean parte de su catálogo.

Los estrenos de series y películas nuevas en Apple TV de esta semana están destacados en amarillo .

¿Cuánto cuesta la suscripción a Apple TV?

La suscripción mensual a Apple TV Plus cuesta $169 pesos al mes, después del periodo de prueba de 7 días.

También te podría interesar los estrenos de:

Estrenos de películas en Apple TV (octubre 2026)

Matchbox: The Movie (Dir. Sam Hargrave, 2026) (09/10/2026)

The Last First: Winter K2 (Dir. Amir Bar-Lev, 2026) (02/10/2026) Una histórica carrera por completar el primer ascenso invernal al K2 se convierte en tragedia, revelando que la ambición humana, el ego y la búsqueda de la gloria pueden ser tan letales como la propia montaña.

Matchbox: The Movie (Dir. Sam Hargrave, 2026) (09/10/2026) Después de que los hostiles secuestran al ex soldado Sean Walker para localizar una ojiva nuclear, la CIA sospecha de su participación. Más tarde, Walker y sus aliados planean recuperar la bomba y limpiar sus nombres.

Tenzing (Dir.a Jennifer Peedom, 2026) (09/10/2026) Tras unirse a una expedición británica, el escalador del Himalaya Tenzing Norgay y el montañista neozelandés Edmund Hillary se convierten en las primeras personas en alcanzar la cima del Monte Everest. Protagonizan Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston y Willem Dafoe.

Estrenos de series en Apple TV (octubre 2026)

Stick: el swing perfecto – Temporada 2 (30/10/2026)

Pequeños profetas (Small Prophet s) (07/10/2026) Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) vive estancado desde la desaparición de su pareja Clea hace siete años. Su padre Brian (Sir Michael Palin) le entrega una receta alquímica para crear homúnculos (espíritus mágicos capaces de predecir el futuro) con la esperanza de saber si volverá a ver a Clea.

Buscando a Wanda (Where’s Wanda?) – Temporada 2 (21/10/2026) Wanda, la hija de Carlotta y Dedo, lleva meses desaparecida sin dejar rastro. Como la policía no llega a ninguna parte, los padres toman la búsqueda en sus propias manos. Utilizan equipos de vigilancia para espiar el barrio.

Nocturno (Nocturn e ) (30/10/2026) ESTRENO EN APPLE TV ESTA SEMANA Cuando una víctima del notorio asesino en serie Jurek Walter aparece inesperadamente con vida, el detective Jonah Lynn corre contra el tiempo para encontrar a la única persona que aún está desaparecida, mientras su protegida Saga Bauer se infiltra para obtener respuestas del propio asesino.

Stick: el swing perfecto – Temporada 2 (30/10/2026) ESTRENO EN APPLE TV ESTA SEMANA Pryce Cahill se encaminaba hacia la grandeza en el golf cuando un colapso en el campo descarriló su carrera; luchando por mantenerse a flote, lo da todo para ser mentor de Santi, un joven prodigio con gran potencial, y tal vez salvarse a sí mismo. Protagonizan Owen Wilson, Mariana Treviño, Marc Maron y Rhea Seehorn.
